label: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE (Fixture Co): invented for testing; no real study, school, classroom or participant.
question: How does adding predict-and-trace prompts before code modification change grade 10 students' code-modification correctness in a four-week Python unit (classroom-a vs classroom-b, fixture)?

rationale.theory: Reading and tracing precede writing in novice programming (Lister et al. 2009; Lopez et al. 2008); use-modify-create sequencing (Franklin et al. 2020).

method.justification: Intact classes cannot be randomized at student level; a nonequivalent-groups design with a pretest covariate answers a causal question with stated threats.
confound_controls: same teacher and unit materials in both classes
pretest on code tracing as covariate
same assessment items and blind double scoring

instruments.name: code-modification tasks
instruments.construct: modifying working code to a new specification
instruments.validity_plan: expert review of item-objective fit; pilot with a non-study class; two raters with a calibration round

instruments.name: tracing pretest
instruments.validity_evidence: items adapted from published tracing tasks; reliability reported after pilot

analysis.plan: ANCOVA on post-unit modification correctness with pretest covariate; report effect size with 95% CI; no subgroup claims without a preregistered hypothesis

ethics.review_body: the district research office and a university IRB, as applicable (to be identified)
ethics.consent_assent: parent or guardian consent and student assent, with a non-participation path that keeps the same instruction
risks: grades must not depend on participation

data_management.storage: district-approved storage only (to be identified by a human)
data_management.deidentification: study IDs replace names before analysis

limitations: two intact classes; results do not generalize beyond them without replication
